title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: law (2015)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for law (2015). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Which one is not a core international human rights treaty?
options: ICCPR
CRC
UDHR
ICESCR
questions.explanation: The UDHR is a declaration, not a treaty.

questions.questionText: Tobar Doctrine is related to?
options: The recognition of state
The recognition of government
The recognition of insurgents
Formation of state
questions.explanation: The Tobar Doctrine pertains to the recognition of governments.

questions.questionText: An uncodified constitution could be taken as an instance of:
options: Flexible Constitution
Rigid Constitution
Republican Constitution
Federal Constitution
questions.explanation: An uncodified constitution is typically flexible.

questions.questionText: For Kant a Maxim is, _________
options: Moral code
condition
prescribed thought process
subjective principle of action
questions.explanation: A maxim is a subjective principle of action according to Kant.

questions.questionText: One of the following principles of taxation advocates that a tax system should not influence the economic decisions of taxpayers.
options: Principle of independence
Principle of neutrality
Principle of certainty
Principle of free decision
questions.explanation: The principle of neutrality states that taxes should not influence economic decisions.

questions.questionText: Identify the non-observance of essential conditions of marriage which causes necessarily the dissolution of marriage.
options: Marriages concluded by judicially interdicted persons
Marriages concluded under the influence of violence
Marriages concluded in the existence of fundamental error
Marriages concluded with person related by consanguinity
questions.explanation: Marriages concluded by judicially interdicted persons are void and cause dissolution.

questions.questionText: Which of the following assertions about human rights limitations and derogations is incorrect?
options: Derogation is a temporary measure, but a limitation is permanent.
Both arise from the fact that most human rights are not absolute.
Both limits and derogations are guided by the criteria of necessity and proportionality.
None
questions.explanation: Derogations are temporary, while limitations can be permanent.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is odd from the others?
options: Ownership
Usufruct
Servitude
Expropriation
questions.explanation: Expropriation is the odd one out because it's a process by which the government takes private property for public use with compensation, while ownership, usufruct, and servitude are all property rights. Ownership is a complete right, but it's not the differentiating factor here.

questions.questionText: For a rule utilitarian an action is always morally right, when _________
options: It conforms to a set of moral rules defined in a rule book.
It is in tune with the greater good for the masses.
The act of the individual is self-indulgent.
It contravenes with the deeply entrenched moral values of the society.
questions.explanation: Rule utilitarianism focuses on actions that promote the greatest good.

questions.questionText: Which one is incorrect about the informal constitutional amendment procedure?
options: Informal constitutional amendment happens by altering the constitutional text
An informal amendment may take place through judicial decisions
The usage of the executive body may give rise to the informal amendment of the Constitution
Informal amendment of the Constitution happens without changing the constitutional text
questions.explanation: The first statement is incorrect because informal constitutional amendments, by definition, occur without changing the actual text of the constitution. Instead, they involve changes in interpretation, application, or understanding of constitutional provisions through judicial decisions, executive actions, or established conventions.

questions.questionText: Which one is true about the making of the Constitution?
options: It is a complex process that involves several stakeholders
Constitution-making needs to reflect shared values
Constitutional making should consider the need for longevity
All
questions.explanation: All options are true regarding the constitution-making process.

questions.questionText: Among the following workers which could be affected first by the reduction of workforce order?
options: Expectant mothers
Those employees with disability
Workers' representatives
Those having fewer dependents
questions.explanation: Typically, those with fewer dependents may be affected first.

questions.questionText: According to Von Savigny the concept of the law is described as:
options: Law is the product of the common consciousness of the society.
Law is emanated from a specified sovereign organ.
The source of the law is not custom but the command of the sovereign.
The sources of the laws are the judges.
questions.explanation: Von Savigny believed law is a product of societal consciousness.

questions.questionText: One of the following is true about a constitution?
options: It is a political document.
It is a legal document.
It limits the power of basic organs of Government.
All
questions.explanation: All options are true regarding the nature of a constitution.

questions.questionText: According to Lon Fuller inner morality of law:
options: Laws shall be made for temporary purpose only
Laws shall be retroactive
Laws shall be intelligible
Laws shall be inconsistent
questions.explanation: Fuller emphasized that laws must be intelligible.

questions.questionText: Which one is the basic rationale that necessitates the HOF as a choice to adjudicate constitutional matters in Ethiopia?
options: The political nature of the FDRE constitution
The legal expertise of the members of house of Federation
The former history of the judiciary
The role played by nation, nationality and people in FDRE constitution
questions.explanation: The role of nations and nationalities is crucial in the FDRE constitution.

questions.questionText: As per the FDRE Constitution, one of the following differs from the others?
options: Supremacy of the Constitution.
Gender equality.
Secularism.
Transparency and accountability of public institutions.
questions.explanation: Supremacy of the Constitution is a foundational principle.

questions.questionText: One of the following statements concerning the FDRE constitution is incorrect?
options: The Constitution is categorized as a Rigid Constitution.
The Bill of Rights chapter of the Constitution incorporates all three generations of human rights.
Regarding rights restrictions, the Constitution contains a general limitations clause.
None
questions.explanation: The FDRE Constitution does not contain a general limitations clause. Instead, it includes specific limitation clauses for individual rights.

questions.questionText: Which one best describes the effect of flagrant offenses?
options: Any person can arrest some suspects without warrant
Any person can arrest some suspects with warrant
Police can arrest any suspect without warrant
Police can arrest any suspect with warrant
questions.explanation: Flagrant offenses (caught in the act) allow any person to make a citizen's arrest without a warrant. This is a universal principle in criminal procedure where immediate action is required when a crime is being committed in plain view.

questions.questionText: One of the following statements concerning constitutional amendments is wrong.
options: While a rigid Constitution may limit required constitutional updates.
Flexible constitutions are amended more frequently than rigid ones.
flexible constitution allows for simple amending requirements.
All
questions.explanation: Rigid constitutions can limit amendments.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an affirmative defense under the FDRE Criminal Code of Ethiopia?
options: Intoxication
Insanity
Infancy
Necessity
questions.explanation: Necessity is an affirmative defense under the FDRE Criminal Code. While insanity is a defense, it is classified as a ground of irresponsibility rather than an affirmative defense per se.

questions.questionText: One of the following is a void treaty:
options: treaty that is formed based on erroneous fact.
treaty that is formed contrary to a jus cogens norm.
treaty that is formed by coercion of representative of a State.
treaty that is contradictory with new jus cogens.
questions.explanation: Treaties contrary to jus cogens norms are void.

questions.questionText: The goal of separation of power is:
options: To do away with or minimize tyranny
To ensure the Liberty of Citizens
Ensuring the efficiency of the Government
All
questions.explanation: All options reflect the goals of separation of powers.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a school of jurisprudence which considers judges as the true law makers?
options: Legal positivism
Stoicism
Legal realism
Feminist Legal theory
questions.explanation: Stoicism does not focus on judges as law makers.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a lawful interest of post-conflict societies in transition process in the aftermath of grave and systematic human rights violations?
options: The interest to know the truth
The interest of justice
The interest of peace and reconciliation
The interest to get Revenge
questions.explanation: Revenge is not a lawful interest in post-conflict societies.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a correct course of action in legal profession according to the application of rule utilitarianism?
options: An act of advocate during his/her professional service is right only if it produces the best interest of the client.
Telling a lie before a court of law may be right as long as it is done to protect the best interests of his client.
Any action of the advocate that fails to protect the best interests of his client is wrong.
An action of the advocate is right only if such action is done in conformity with the advocate's code of conduct regulation.
questions.explanation: Actions must conform to the advocate's code of conduct.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is different among the given alternatives?
options: Strict liability
Liability without fault
Liability which does not depend on actual negligence or intent to harm
Vicarious liability
questions.explanation: Vicarious liability is fundamentally different because it involves liability for the actions of another person (holding someone responsible for another's actions), while the other options all describe forms of liability regardless of fault on the part of the primary actor.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not true about international law applied at the international level and international law applied in domestic courts?
options: The domestic laws of Ethiopia are not relevant in deciding Ethiopia's international obligations in disputes before international tribunals.
Nation in an international court generally may use its domestic laws as an excuse to alter its international obligations.
The domestic laws of Ethiopia are extremely important in determining how international laws will apply in the domestic courts of Ethiopia.
Domestic courts often refer to treaties (and international customs) when deciding disputes between the individual litigants before them.
questions.explanation: The second statement is false. According to Article 27 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, a nation cannot invoke provisions of its internal law as justification for its failure to perform a treaty obligation. Nations cannot use domestic laws as an excuse to alter international obligations.

questions.questionText: In the absence of contract of marriage or where contract of marriage is invalid under the law, one of the following is a common property:
options: The property which the spouse possesses on the day of their marriage
The property which a spouse acquires by succession after marriage
All property acquired by spouse during marriage by onerous title
Property which a spouse acquires by donation after their marriage
questions.explanation: All property acquired during marriage is considered common property.

questions.questionText: Which one is the main purpose of probation in employment?
options: To test the suitability of the employee
To ensure the benefit of employee
To determine the cost of employment
To validate the contract of employment
questions.explanation: The main purpose of probation is to assess employee suitability.

questions.questionText: One of the following statements is not true about the applicability of the Civil Code on the status and activities of traders.
options: The Civil Code provisions of general contract law apply to the formation of contracts between traders
The Commercial Code is a self-contained law on traders and there is no need for the application of the Civil Code on traders
The applicability of the Civil Code on traders can be excluded if otherwise provided in the Commercial Code
The Civil Code provisions other than the general contract law can also apply to traders
questions.explanation: The Commercial Code is not entirely self-contained.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not necessarily relevant in determining the amount of bail:
options: The seriousness of the crime
The criminal record of the accused
The financial status of the accused
The social ties of the defendant
questions.explanation: Social ties of the defendant are actually often considered in bail determinations as they relate to flight risk, but they are generally not as directly relevant to determining the specific amount of bail as the other factors listed, which are more explicitly prescribed in bail determination statutes.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following aspects typically characterizes a joint venture form of business organization under the Ethiopian law?
options: It is not required to be registered
It can be managed by one partner
It is useful, especially for wealthy people who want to carry out business secretly
If its existence is disclosed, it is regarded as a general partnership
questions.explanation: A disclosed joint venture is treated as a general partnership.

questions.questionText: Which of the following claims, out of the alternatives, is false?
options: The only form of compensation under Ethiopian tort law is monetary compensation.
The existence or absence of intention is never relevant under Ethiopian law when determining whether the defendant is at fault.
The Ethiopian Law of Strict Liability prohibits the assessment of fault on the part of either of the parties in a tort.
questions.explanation: The claim that monetary compensation is the only form of compensation under Ethiopian tort law is false. Ethiopian tort law also recognizes other remedies such as injunctions, specific performance, and restitution in appropriate cases.

questions.questionText: The goal of separation of power is:
options: To do away with or minimize tyranny
To ensure the Liberty of Citizens
Ensuring the efficiency of the Government
All
questions.explanation: All options reflect the goals of separation of powers.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not correct about constitutional interpretation?
options: It aims at extracting the general normative content of the written Constitution
It seeks to identify the meaning of the constitutional provision
It solely assigns certain meanings to the constitutional text
It is the activity of maintaining constitutional supremacy
questions.explanation: The third statement is incorrect. Constitutional interpretation doesn't 'solely' assign meanings to the text - it's a complex process that involves extracting meaning, considering context, history, purpose, and normative content while respecting constitutional supremacy. It's not a one-dimensional assignment of meaning.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following business organizations contains both limited partners and general partners together?
options: General partnership
Private limited company
Joint Venture
Limited Partnership
questions.explanation: A Limited Partnership includes both types of partners.

questions.questionText: A share is a financial asset to the shareholder.
options: Share is a financial asset to the shareholder.
Share gives rights to the holder.
Shareholder is a part-owner of the company.
All
questions.explanation: All statements about shares are true.

questions.questionText: Contracting parties have complete 'freedom to carry out' any of the following acts, with the exception of:
options: Choosing the appropriate payment method.
Establishing the location, timing, and manner of the contract's performance.
Providing a grace period to a non-performing party.
Determining a contract's requirements regarding the legality of a contract.
questions.explanation: Parties cannot have complete freedom to determine legality requirements of a contract, as these are established by law and public policy. The other options fall within the legitimate scope of party autonomy in contract formation and execution.

questions.questionText: One of the following matters is not required by the Commercial Code to be indicated by the Memorandum of Association?
options: The capital of the company
The general manager of the company
The business purpose of the company
The head office of the company
questions.explanation: The general manager is not a required detail in the Memorandum.

questions.questionText: Efficiency of taxation is often measured against the following costs, except:
options: Administrative costs
Externality cost
Compliance costs
Excess costs
questions.explanation: Externality costs are not typically a measure of tax efficiency.

questions.questionText: Shares in a private limited company:
options: Are freely transferred among their shareholders
Need a majority vote of at least 75% to transfer them to outsiders
Shall be transmitted to the heirs of the shareholders
All
questions.explanation: Shares in a private limited company have restrictions on transfer.

questions.questionText: The principle of legality comprises all but not one of the following doctrines?
options: Principle of maximum certainty of crimes and penalties.
Principle of double effect of euthanasia.
Principle of strict interpretation and prohibition of analogy.
Prohibition of double jeopardy.
questions.explanation: The principle of double effect of euthanasia is not part of the principle of legality in criminal law. The principle of legality (nullum crimen, nulla poena sine lege) includes the other listed doctrines: legal certainty, strict interpretation, and protection against double jeopardy.

questions.questionText: Which one best describes the effect of flagrant offenses?
options: Any person can arrest some suspects without warrant
Any person can arrest some suspects with warrant
Police can arrest any suspect without warrant
Police can arrest any suspect with warrant
questions.explanation: In the case of flagrant offenses (where the offense is being committed or has just been committed), any person has the legal right to arrest the suspect without a warrant. This citizen's arrest power is limited to situations where immediate action is necessary.

Flexible constitutions are amended more frequently than rigid ones.
flexible constitution allows for simple amending requirements.
All
questions.explanation: Rigid constitutions can limit amendments.

treaty that is formed by coercion of representative of a State.
treaty that is contradictory with new jus cogens.
questions.explanation: Treaties contrary to jus cogens norms are void.

The social ties of the defendant

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not true about the object of property rights under the Ethiopian law?
options: It is not necessary for a good to have an economic value to be property at law.
Goods under the civil code of Ethiopia should be understood to mean anything capable of human appropriation whether it is tangible or intangible.

Anything whose source is not traced back to the labor, capital, creativity and enterprise of individual citizen or associations which enjoy juridical personality is not recognized as property rights under the Ethiopian property law.
None.
questions.explanation: Option D indicates that none of the statements are false.

questions.questionText: One of the following statements is true about the concept of ownership.
options: Ownership is an absolute right and it is not subjected to limitation of any form.
It may be the case that persons having subordinate rights on a particular object may exclude the owner of such object.
Ownership is always perpetual in nature.
Ownership may in no cases be dismembered.
questions.explanation: Option B is true as subordinate rights can limit the owner's rights.

questions.questionText: Which statement is true about the scope of the law of property?
options: The law of property governs all a person's legal rights, of whatever description.
All proprietary rights as opposed to personal rights are the object of the law of property.
The law of property is the law of proprietary rights in rem, the law of proprietary rights in personnem being distinguished from it as the law of obligations.
None.
questions.explanation: Option C correctly distinguishes between proprietary rights in rem and in personam.

questions.questionText: Which statement is true about possession under the Ethiopian laws?
options: person may have possession of an object without physically controlling the object.
person may not possess an immovable property as it is impossible to have physical control of the immovable.
The law of possession does not apply to incorporeal things.
Possession may not be transferred without the actual handing over of a thing.
questions.explanation: Option A is true as possession can exist without physical control.

questions.questionText: Identify the correct statement about expropriation under the current constitutional order.
options: Public interest/purpose is defined in terms of direct or indirect benefit derived from use of a property.
Courts are not allowed to review whether the public purpose requirement is satisfied.
Compensation decided by experts cannot be reviewed by courts.
The measure of compensation for private property in expropriation of land holding is market value.
C&D.
questions.explanation: Option A is correct. Under the current Ethiopian constitutional framework, public interest/purpose in expropriation is defined broadly in terms of direct or indirect benefit derived from the use of property. This broad definition gives the government significant discretion in determining what constitutes 'public purpose.' Options C and D are incorrect - courts can review compensation decisions, and compensation for land is not based on market value since land is owned by the state.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not true about classification of goods in movable and immovable.
options: The classification of objects into movable and immovable is purely a matter of policy choice adopted by the state.
Goods are classified in movable and immovable according to their importance to the community.
The FDRE Constitution relegates the categorization of things into movable and immovable to secondary importance.
The legal rules governing property under the Ethiopian civil code reflect the division of things in movable and immovable.
questions.explanation: Option C is incorrect as the Constitution does not prioritize this classification.

questions.questionText: Mr. A is a military commander. Mr. B, a man of integrity is a public servant heading procurement department. Mr. B's office floated a bid to procure stationery for the office. One of the bidders happened to be Mr. A's friend. Mr. A called Mr. B and told him to allot the bid to his friend. Mr. B feared what could happen to him and declared Mr. A's friend winner. Based on this fact:
options: Mr. B can escape fault based extra-contractual liability invoking superior order.
Mr. B cannot escape liability because there is no hierarchical relationship between Mr. A and B.
Mr. A will be subjected to fault based liability and cannot get any mitigation on quantum of compensation.
and B are answers.
and C are answers.
questions.explanation: Options B and C are correct. Mr. B cannot escape liability as there is no hierarchical relationship between him and Mr. A (they work in different departments). Additionally, Mr. A will be subject to fault-based liability without mitigation since he abused his position to influence the procurement process.

questions.questionText: In establishing a fault based liability according to article 2030:
options: The mental status of defendant is considered to establish liability.
Reasonable man is the standard to assess the conduct of any defendant.
personal circumstances, exposures, and education status are all taken into consideration.
Mental status of a defendant is taken into consideration to assess damages.
All of the above are answers.
questions.explanation: All options are relevant in establishing fault based liability.

questions.questionText: Danny and Richo were running to catch a bus. Danny stumbled on Richo's feet. She wants to sue for physical assault under article 2038. Which elements have to be fulfilled to establish her case?
options: Intention of the defendant.
Physical contact.
Negligence of the defendant.
That the contact is done without the consent of the plaintiff.
All except C.
All of the above.
questions.explanation: Option E (All except C) is correct. To establish a case of physical assault under Article 2038, the plaintiff must prove: (1) intention of the defendant (mens rea), (2) physical contact (actus reus), and (4) lack of consent for the contact. Negligence (option C) is not a required element for assault, which is an intentional tort. Assault requires intent rather than negligence, making option C the exception.

questions.questionText: Mr. A, an individual with a big chunk of followers on Facebook, is known for posting financial and personal information he claims to be secrets of government officials. He believes that his informants give him true information. On a certain day he posted false information about one high-ranking government official. This time, that government official sued him for tarnishing his reputation. What are the possible defenses?
options: He can claim that he had no intent to injure the official.
He can claim that he has public interest in mind, thus, his posts get protection according to freedom of speech provisions in the FDRE Constitution.
He can retract the post and make another post that he distributed false information.
All of the above.
questions.explanation: All options represent possible defenses against the lawsuit.

questions.questionText: Among the following identify the correct statement about change of venue and removal of judges?
options: Both the plaintiff and the defendant have unhindered right to request change of venue.
An application claiming change of venue must be instituted to the court hearing the suit by the plaintiff.
Parties claiming to removal of judges may not be forced to state the grounds why they are requesting.
court change of venue claimed shall order the suit to be entertained by other court which has material jurisdiction.
All.
questions.explanation: All options correctly describe the procedures regarding change of venue and removal of judges.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is wrong about service of summon and its effect?
options: summon sent to an agent appointed by the defendant on rule of general agency is sufficient to establish jurisdiction on the suit.
service of summon sent to an agent in charge of administration an automobile in the suit for recovery of immovable property is sufficient to establish jurisdiction.

service of summon sent to a manager or an agent carries business work for the defendant who is living in the local limits of the jurisdiction of the court is sufficient to establish jurisdiction upon the defendant.
All of the above.
None of the above.
questions.explanation: Option B is incorrect. A service of summon sent to an agent in charge of administering an automobile would not be sufficient to establish jurisdiction in a suit for recovery of immovable property, as the agent's authority is limited to matters related to the automobile, not immovable property.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about third party defendant?
options: Acceptance of the application of the defendant outrightly makes the third party defendant to be party to the suit.
Third party defendant directly obliged to give his contribution/indemnity to the plaintiff.
The defendant can withdraw the third party defendant from the suit at all.
There are no procedural rules for the third party defendant to present his defence against the plaintiff directly.
None of the above.
questions.explanation: None of the options are correct about third party defendants. A third party defendant doesn't automatically become a party to the suit upon application acceptance - judicial approval is required. They are not directly obliged to compensate the plaintiff but may be obliged to indemnify the defendant. The defendant cannot unilaterally withdraw the third party once joined. And procedural rules do exist for third party defendants to present defenses both against the defendant's claims and sometimes directly against the plaintiff.

questions.questionText: The court is hearing evidences in the suit between the plaintiff Mr. A and the defendant Mr. B. However, Mr. X who has an interest on the case instituted his application of intervention. What will be the order of the court?
options: Without staying the proceeding shall allow the intervention.
Order the intervening party to institute an independent statement of claim.
Order the intervention when separate statement containing all grounds are filled.
copy of statement need not be served to the parties and the court simply proceeds.
If the intervention is made before execution, the court shall still consider the application.
questions.explanation: The court may allow the intervention without staying the proceedings.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is incorrect about the law of pre-trial hearing in Ethiopia?
options: It mainly involves examination of parties and not of evidence.
It has the major purpose of resolving the issues.
It involves ruling on preliminary objections.
It has the main purpose of framing issues, if any.
and B.
questions.explanation: Options A and B are incorrect regarding the purpose of pre-trial hearings.

questions.questionText: Indicate the statement to which you disagree:
options: Plaintiff always makes its opening statement and produces its evidence before defendant does.
Only the judge who rendered the judgement is authorized to pronounce it, otherwise the judgement is null and void.
The court may at any stage recall a witness who has been already examined.
The application to set-aside a proceeding on grounds of procedural irregularity shall be filed to the appellate court.
All except A and C.
questions.explanation: Options A and C are correct statements about court procedure. The plaintiff generally makes its opening statement and produces evidence first (A), and the court can recall a witness who has already been examined (C). The other statements contain inaccuracies: a judge other than the one who rendered judgment can pronounce it (B), and applications to set aside proceedings based on procedural irregularities are typically filed with the court that issued the judgment, not directly to an appellate court (D).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a mechanism of review of judgment by court of rendition?
options: Opposition.
Procedural irregularities.
Clerical or arithmetical mistakes in the judgment.
Discovery of new evidence after rendition of judgment.
All.
questions.explanation: Option D - 'Discovery of new evidence after rendition of judgment' is not typically a mechanism for review by the court of rendition (the court that rendered the original judgment). While opposition (objection to default judgments), correction of procedural irregularities, and correction of clerical/arithmetical errors can be handled by the original court, discovery of new evidence typically requires appeal or a separate application for review to a higher court under most legal systems.

questions.questionText: Which one of the statement is true about issues?
options: Whenever there is a civil suit, it is mandatory for the court to frame an issue or issues.
If a case contains both legal and factual issues, the judge is expected to resolve the factual issues first and then the legal issues.
Issues are framed only by judge under all circumstances.
There might be circumstances where a decision may be made without framing an issue or issues.
civil suit is expected to contain either a legal issues or factual issues.
questions.explanation: Option D is true as decisions can be made without framing issues.

questions.questionText: The potential outcomes of an appellate review are:
options: Variation of the lower court's decision;
Reversal of the lower court's decision;
Referral to the cassation bench if it has basic errors in law.
Confirmation of the lower court's decision;
All.
questions.explanation: All options represent potential outcomes of an appellate review.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not included among factors that break chain of causation?
options: Existence of previous causes.
Existence of concurrent causes.
The act of accomplice causes.
Intervention of extraneous causes.
None.
questions.explanation: None of the options are incorrect - all listed factors (previous causes, concurrent causes, accomplice acts, and intervention of extraneous causes) can potentially break the chain of causation in determining liability.

questions.questionText: According to ---------------------- principle, crimes committed in foreign countries on Ethiopian citizens may be tried in Ethiopia.
options: Principle of territoriality.
Principle of passive nationality.
Principle of active personality.
Principle of universality.
None.
questions.explanation: The principle of passive nationality (Option B) allows a country to assert jurisdiction over crimes committed against its citizens abroad. This differs from the principle of territoriality (crimes committed within a nation's territory), active personality (crimes committed by a nation's citizens abroad), and universality (jurisdiction over certain crimes regardless of connection to the prosecuting state).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following criminal principle is included in Fetha Negest, as mentioned by Graven?
options: Intention and negligence.
Money laundry.
Corruption.
All.
None.
questions.explanation: Intention and negligence are principles included in Fetha Negest.

questions.questionText: Statement one: - According to FDRE criminal code a juridical person except government administrative organs are accountable to all types of crimes. Statement two: - According to FDRE criminal code a juridical person can participate in crimes as Principal criminal, An instigator or an accomplice.
options: Both statements are true.
Both statements are false.
Only statement one is true.
Only statement two is true.
None.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true regarding the accountability of juridical persons.

questions.questionText: One is not among the tests used in identification of the stage of Attempt from preparatory act.
options: Reasonable Inference test.
Sine qua non test.
The commencement of execution test.
Proximity test.
None.
questions.explanation: Option B - 'Sine qua non test' is not typically used to distinguish attempt from preparatory acts in criminal law. The other tests listed (Reasonable Inference, commencement of execution, and proximity tests) are commonly used to determine when preparatory acts cross the threshold to become criminal attempts.

questions.questionText: What necessitate the enactment of the 2004 FDRE criminal code?
options: Legal lacuna.
To redefine purpose and objective of the criminal law.
To increase punishment for some offences.
All of the above.
Only A and B.
questions.explanation: All options contributed to the need for the new criminal code.

questions.questionText: One of the following is odd /unique/ from the rest.
options: Acts allowed by law.
Acts justifiable by law.
Acts forbidden by law.
Acts commanded by law.
None.
questions.explanation: Option C 'Acts forbidden by law' is unique from the rest. While options A, B, and D all refer to lawful acts (allowed, justifiable, or commanded), option C refers to prohibited acts.
